project.name: Political Alpha Tracker
project.description: Research pipeline that matches India's disclosed electoral bonds to NSE-listed companies and tests whether bond buyers lead their peers' returns or moved on the disclosure, using pre-declared statistical tests.

nodes.name: audit_candidates.py
nodes.summary: Command-line helper that lists electoral bond purchasers still needing a manual decision in data/match_audit.csv: the largest unmatched buyers, near-miss names under looser fuzzy rules, and names the strict match rejected.

nodes.name: candidates
nodes.summary: Finds audit candidates not yet decided by combining the top unmatched purchasers, close names under looser scoring and strict-match rejects, and reports the share of unattributed money the top group holds.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Loads the bonds, companies and audit table, then prints the undecided purchasers with their amounts and best candidate names.

nodes.name: connections.py
nodes.summary: Attributes electoral bonds to listed companies through strict name matching, the donor-CIN table and the manual audit, then summarises each company's purchases at entity or group level. This table defines which companies count as connected for every downstream study.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Reduces a company or purchaser name to lower-case boilerplate-free text, reading periods between letters as spaces and joining spaced initials.

nodes.name: load_match_audit
nodes.summary: Reads the manual audit table and rejects unknown decisions or purchasers listed twice.

nodes.name: match_names
nodes.summary: Maps donor names to company keys by fuzzy score plus an exact leading-word rule, and returns rejected candidates, including names shared by two listed companies, for review.

nodes.name: attribute
nodes.summary: Produces one row per bond and company using name, donor-CIN and audit routes, with audit decisions overriding the other two and subsidiaries counted only at group level.

nodes.name: connections
nodes.summary: Aggregates attributed bonds into one row per listed company with totals, dates, purchaser spellings, subsidiary amount and a connected flag based on the largest bond.

nodes.name: bonds.py
nodes.summary: Loads the SBI electoral bond disclosure into a clean table with one row per bond, giving purchaser, rupee amount, purchase date and year.

nodes.name: load_bond_purchases
nodes.summary: Parses the disclosure CSV, converts denominations and purchase dates, and drops rows with no purchaser or no positive amount.

nodes.name: companies.py
nodes.summary: Loads the listed-company universe and the donor-to-CIN table, and defines a company's identity key as its CIN, else BSE scrip code, else ISIN.

nodes.name: load_companies
nodes.summary: Reads the listed-company universe as strings, one row per company.

nodes.name: load_donor_cins
nodes.summary: Reads the table mapping purchaser spellings to the CIN of the listed company they name.

nodes.name: company_key
nodes.summary: Returns a company's identity as its CIN, falling back to scrip code and then ISIN, so share classes under one CIN count as one company.

nodes.name: graph.py
nodes.summary: Builds a NetworkX graph linking bond-buying companies to a single Electoral Bonds node and to their sectors, and renders it as interactive HTML or a static radial PNG.

nodes.name: build_graph
nodes.summary: Creates the graph with company nodes carrying purchase details, one shared bonds node, and sector nodes for companies that have a sector label.

nodes.name: _crore
nodes.summary: Formats a rupee amount as a string in crore.

nodes.name: display_name
nodes.summary: Shortens a company name for display by removing a trailing Limited or Ltd and title-casing all-capital names.

nodes.name: _size
nodes.summary: Returns a node's HTML display size, growing with the square root of the amount a company bought.

nodes.name: save_html
nodes.summary: Writes a self-contained interactive pyvis graph with hover details, patching the tooltip style so line breaks display.

nodes.name: radial_layout
nodes.summary: Computes deterministic positions with the bonds node at the centre, sectors on an outer ring, their companies fanned in front, and unlabelled companies on an inner ring.

nodes.name: save_png
nodes.summary: Renders the static README graph with area-scaled markers, numbered largest buyers, sector labels and a legend, in dark or light theme.

nodes.name: lead_lag.py
nodes.summary: Splits each sector into connected, size-matched placebo and peer groups and computes their equal-weight return baskets for the peer lead-lag test. The placebo leaders are removed from the peers so a group cannot predict itself.

nodes.name: SectorGroups
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding one sector's connected, placebo and peer symbols, with a check that each group meets its minimum size.

nodes.name: LeadLagTest
nodes.summary: Holds the price store, company universe and connected set, and builds sector groups and periodic return baskets for the study's regressions.

nodes.name: build_groups
nodes.summary: Screens companies by liquidity and splits each sector into connected names, placebo leaders closest to the connected median traded value, and the remaining peers.

nodes.name: figures.py
nodes.summary: Generates the README figures in light and dark variants: the connection graph, lead-lag coefficients with intervals, event-study abnormal returns, and growth of the weekly trading rule.

nodes.name: _axes
nodes.summary: Creates a themed figure and axes with shared spine, tick and grid styling.

nodes.name: _save
nodes.summary: Saves a figure on its theme background, creating the directory first, and closes it.

nodes.name: lead_lag_chart
nodes.summary: Plots treatment, placebo and difference coefficients with 95% intervals for each pre-declared specification.

nodes.name: event_chart
nodes.summary: Plots buyers' cumulative abnormal return minus matched controls around each event, with a 95% band under no reaction.

nodes.name: rule_chart
nodes.summary: Plots growth of one rupee for the weekly rule before and after costs and for buy-and-hold, annotated with Sharpe ratios.

nodes.name: lead_lag_rows
nodes.summary: Builds the chart rows of treatment, placebo and difference estimates for each specification in the study grid.

nodes.name: save_all
nodes.summary: Computes every study input and writes all four figures in both themes, returning the paths written.

nodes.name: lead_lag.py
nodes.summary: Runs the pre-declared peer lead-lag study over four frequency and lag specifications, fitting treatment and placebo arms and testing their difference with period-clustered standard errors and Holm-adjusted decision rules.

nodes.name: _pool
nodes.summary: Builds sector-period observations with baskets demeaned within sector, adding lagged connected, placebo, peer and market returns.

nodes.name: _estimate
nodes.summary: Extracts one term's coefficient, standard error, t, p, 95% interval and minimum detectable effect from a fitted model.

nodes.name: stacked_difference
nodes.summary: Fits both arms in one fully interacted regression clustered by date, so the interaction term is treatment minus placebo with a standard error that accounts for shared dates.

nodes.name: pooled_fit
nodes.summary: Fits the treatment arm, placebo arm and their difference for one frequency and lag specification.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the study at group and entity level, then repeats the group level with liquidity judged on 2019 traded value as a later check.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Runs the specification grid for one definition of connected, prints sample sizes and estimates, and applies the Holm-adjusted decision rules.

nodes.name: test_bonds.py
nodes.summary: Tests the bond loader on a small synthetic CSV and checks the committed disclosure against its known row count, total amount, purchaser count and date range.

nodes.name: test_parses_rows_and_skips_blank_ones
nodes.summary: Checks that a synthetic file with a byte-order mark, padded names, a blank row and comma-grouped amounts parses correctly.

nodes.name: test_committed_disclosure_loads_completely
nodes.summary: Pins the committed disclosure's bond count, total amount, purchaser count, denominations and date range.

nodes.name: test_lead_lag.py
nodes.summary: Tests sector group construction, especially that placebo leaders stay disjoint from peers and connected firms, and checks that the stacked regression matches separate fits and detects only a genuine difference.

nodes.name: universe
nodes.summary: Builds a test company table in the shape of data/companies.csv from minimal rows.

nodes.name: make_setup
nodes.summary: Creates a seeded random price panel with four connected and twelve unconnected symbols in one sector.

nodes.name: FakeStore
nodes.summary: In-memory stand-in for the price store that returns fixed closes and traded values.

nodes.name: TestGroupConstruction
nodes.summary: Tests group identification, placebo disjointness from peers and connected firms, traded-value matching and skipping of thin sectors.

nodes.name: TestDifferenceTest
nodes.summary: Tests that the stacked regression reproduces separate fits and flags a real difference while ignoring a shared leader effect.

nodes.name: test_placebo_matches_connected_on_traded_value
nodes.summary: Checks that the placebo leaders chosen are the two names closest to the connected group's traded value.

nodes.name: test_sector_with_too_few_connected_is_skipped
nodes.summary: Checks that a sector with only one connected company produces no groups.

nodes.name: _pool
nodes.summary: Generates a synthetic pooled panel where both leaders share a common factor and the connected leader can carry an extra effect on peers.

nodes.name: price_store.py
nodes.summary: Local Parquet-cached panel of split- and dividend-adjusted NSE closes and raw volume, fetched in batches from yfinance. Removes implausible price moves and serves point-in-time liquidity figures to the studies.
nodes.languageNotes: The yfinance fetch is isolated in a static _download method so the data source can be swapped without touching the rest of the module.

nodes.name: factor_backtest.py
nodes.summary: Long-only cross-sectional factor backtester with per-trade NSE delivery costs, T+1 execution and random or liquidity selection controls. Also provides the shared return metrics, an append-only trial log, the block-bootstrap Sharpe interval and the deflated Sharpe ratio.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dataclasses for CostModel and BacktestResult, and imports FactorEngine and arch.bootstrap lazily inside the functions that need them.

nodes.name: controls.py
nodes.summary: Study that tests whether factor selection beats liquidity-only and multi-seed random selection from the same universe, then repeats the check over the longest window the panel supports. Prints a Phase 3 proceed-or-stop verdict.

nodes.name: factor.py
nodes.summary: Phase 2 validation study that runs a pre-declared grid of factor configurations and logs every trial. Evaluates the best result by bootstrap interval, deflated Sharpe, equal-weight excess and in-sample sub-periods to decide the gate.

nodes.name: leadlag_rule.py
nodes.summary: Study of whether the size lead-lag can be traded: holds a peer basket only after liquid leaders rose and compares the result after costs with buy-and-hold of the same basket. Baskets are re-formed point in time, and the monthly gap is tested with a paired bootstrap.

nodes.name: test_factor_backtest.py
nodes.summary: Tests that the block-bootstrap Sharpe interval is reproducible across runs and that the deflated Sharpe ratio falls as the trial count rises.

nodes.name: test_leadlag_rule.py
nodes.summary: Regression tests for the lead-lag rule covering point-in-time basket membership, once-only round-trip cost charging and a seeded paired bootstrap.

nodes.name: test_price_store.py
nodes.summary: Tests for price-panel cleaning of bad prints and unadjusted splits, the trailing point-in-time liquidity history, and the cleaned-versus-raw close accessor, using a temporary Parquet fixture.

nodes.name: remove_impossible_moves
nodes.summary: Chain-links out close-to-close moves beyond a limit by zeroing them and rescaling earlier prices, returning the cleaned panel and the removed moves.

nodes.name: PriceStore
nodes.summary: Reads, updates and merges the cached close and volume panels, exposing cleaned closes, as-of average daily traded value, rolling liquidity history and coverage statistics.

nodes.name: CostModel
nodes.summary: Dataclass of NSE delivery charges (STT, exchange, SEBI, stamp duty, GST, DP charge, slippage) that computes buy, sell and round-trip percentage costs.

nodes.name: sharpe_ratio
nodes.summary: Annualised Sharpe ratio of periodic returns with no risk-free rate, returning 0 when undefined.

nodes.name: cagr
nodes.summary: Compound annual growth rate of a periodic return series.

nodes.name: max_drawdown
nodes.summary: Largest fall of the compounded return curve from its running peak, as a negative fraction.

nodes.name: BacktestResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding net, gross and benchmark returns, turnover and holdings of a run, with methods for Sharpe, annual return, drawdown, cost drag and a summary dictionary.

nodes.name: TrialLog
nodes.summary: Append-only JSONL record of every backtested configuration, supplying the trial count that makes the deflated Sharpe ratio meaningful.

nodes.name: bootstrap_sharpe_ci
nodes.summary: Seeded stationary block-bootstrap confidence interval for the annualised Sharpe, using arch BCa with a manual percentile fallback.

nodes.name: deflated_sharpe_ratio
nodes.summary: Bailey and Lopez de Prado deflated Sharpe ratio, giving the probability a daily Sharpe beats the best of n noise trials and flagging a 0.95 pass.

nodes.name: FactorBacktest
nodes.summary: Simulates rebalanced equal-weight portfolios chosen by factor, liquidity or random selection, charging costs at each rebalance and logging each run as a trial.

nodes.name: _row
nodes.summary: Formats one backtest summary as a fixed-width report line.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the factor, liquidity and seeded random backtests on both windows, computes the bootstrap interval and deflated Sharpe, and prints the verdict.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the pre-declared grid, picks the best net Sharpe, and prints its interval, deflated Sharpe, sub-period Sharpes and the three-part Phase 2 gate.

nodes.name: stats
nodes.summary: Summarises a return series as Sharpe, annual return, drawdown and count, returning zeros for short or constant series.

nodes.name: trading_costs
nodes.summary: Per-period cost of a long-or-cash position, charging the buy side on entry and the sell side on exit.

nodes.name: paired_bootstrap
nodes.summary: Seeded stationary block bootstrap of the rule's Sharpe minus buy-and-hold's, resampling the same periods for both series.

nodes.name: basket_groups
nodes.summary: Assigns leader and peer membership per period from the traded value known at its start.

nodes.name: basket_returns
nodes.summary: Computes equal-weight leader and peer basket returns per period, with membership re-formed from prior sessions and name counts.

nodes.name: weekly_curves
nodes.summary: Weekly returns of the threshold-zero rule gross and net of costs alongside buy-and-hold, for the results figure.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Evaluates the rule at each threshold and frequency against buy-and-hold, then prints the paired bootstrap and the verdict.

nodes.name: _returns
nodes.summary: Builds a seeded normal daily return series for the statistics tests.

nodes.name: test_the_bootstrap_interval_is_the_same_on_every_run
nodes.summary: Checks that two bootstrap intervals on the same series are identical and bracket the point Sharpe.

nodes.name: test_more_trials_deflate_the_same_sharpe_ratio_further
nodes.summary: Checks that 200 trials raise the expected noise Sharpe and lower the deflated Sharpe compared with 2 trials.

nodes.name: test_baskets_use_only_the_traded_value_known_at_the_time
nodes.summary: Checks leader and peer membership follows the traded value known at each period, as a stock rises in liquidity or lists later.

nodes.name: test_a_round_trip_pays_buy_and_sell_once
nodes.summary: Checks that entering and exiting a position costs exactly one round trip.

nodes.name: test_holding_from_the_first_period_pays_the_buy_side
nodes.summary: Checks that a position held from the first period is charged the buy side only once.

nodes.name: test_the_paired_bootstrap_gives_the_same_interval_on_every_run
nodes.summary: Checks that the paired bootstrap repeats exactly under one seed and differs under another.

nodes.name: _panel
nodes.summary: Builds a small float price panel on business days from column keyword arguments.

nodes.name: test_a_bad_print_that_reverts_leaves_no_trace
nodes.summary: Checks that a huge one-day print and its reversal are both removed while the latest price stays untouched.

nodes.name: test_an_unadjusted_split_is_rescaled_not_a_crash
nodes.summary: Checks that an unadjusted halving rescales earlier prices and records one removed move.

nodes.name: test_moves_within_the_limit_gaps_and_other_symbols_are_kept
nodes.summary: Checks that moves within the limit survive, that gaps stay missing, and that moves across gaps are measured from the last close.

nodes.name: store
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that writes temporary close and volume Parquet files, redirects the module paths to them and returns a PriceStore.

nodes.name: test_adv_history_is_trailing_and_waits_for_min_periods
nodes.summary: Checks the rolling traded value in crore and that it stays missing until min_periods sessions exist.

nodes.name: test_close_is_cleaned_by_default_and_raw_on_request
nodes.summary: Checks that close() strips a written bad print by default and returns it when clean=False.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central constants for the study: project and data paths, input file locations, and the fixed rules that define a politically connected company (attribution level, name-match threshold, minimum bond size, price panel end date).

nodes.name: build_companies.py
nodes.summary: Rebuilds data/companies.csv, the listed-company universe, from committed NSE equity, Nifty Total Market, company ID and earlier sector files, assigning CINs, scrip codes and macro-sector labels.

nodes.name: test_build_companies.py
nodes.summary: Tests that the universe builder reproduces the committed companies.csv, maps every index industry to one of 12 macro sectors, and preserves the earlier universe's company keys.

nodes.name: test_connections.py
nodes.summary: Tests attribution of electoral bonds to listed companies, covering false and missed name matches, aggregation across every bond, donor CIN routes, and audit decisions at entity and group level.

nodes.name: _read
nodes.summary: Reads a CSV as strings with blanks preserved and strips whitespace from column names and every value.

nodes.name: _lookup
nodes.summary: Fetches a column from a reference table for each company, matching by ISIN first and NSE symbol second, and returning an empty string when neither matches.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Assembles the universe from every equity on NSE's list, joining identifiers and sector labels, and raises ValueError if an index industry has no macro-sector mapping.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the builder, writes the result to the companies file, and prints the company count and how many have a sector label.

nodes.name: test_every_industry_in_the_index_file_has_a_macro_sector
nodes.summary: Checks that every industry in the Nifty Total Market file is mapped in MACRO_SECTOR and that the mapping yields exactly 12 macro sectors.

nodes.name: test_the_committed_universe_is_what_the_builder_makes
nodes.summary: Checks that the committed companies.csv is identical to a fresh build from the raw inputs.

nodes.name: test_the_universe_is_nse_list_and_keys_are_unique_per_listing
nodes.summary: Checks that the universe's ISINs equal NSE's list, that no company key is blank, and that rows sharing a key all carry a non-blank CIN.

nodes.name: test_earlier_companies_keep_their_keys
nodes.summary: Checks that every company from the earlier universe is found by ISIN or symbol and retains its original CIN.

nodes.name: companies
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a company table in the shape of data/companies.csv from scrip, name, CIN and sector tuples.

nodes.name: bonds
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a bond purchases table from purchaser, amount and date tuples, with parsed dates and a year column.

nodes.name: audit
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a match-audit table from purchaser, decision and NSE symbol tuples.

nodes.name: TestNameMatching
nodes.summary: Tests the strict name matcher: the leading-word rule, boilerplate removal, joined initials, refusal of weak matches, and scrip-code keys for companies without a CIN.

nodes.name: TestConnections
nodes.summary: Tests the connections table: every bond is aggregated, the minimum bond rule applies, donor CINs fill matching gaps, and bonds found by both routes count once.

nodes.name: TestMatchingFixes
nodes.summary: Regression tests for periods between letters in names and for names that two listed companies share, which must be refused.

nodes.name: TestAudit
nodes.summary: Tests audit decisions: same-company rows count at both levels, subsidiaries count only at group level, and not_attributed vetoes a name match.

nodes.name: delisting_registry.py
nodes.summary: Holds NSE's real delisting record, separates failures from buyouts, and estimates the annual return drag that a survivors-only price panel omits. Backtests use it to report how far their figures are overstated, since the missing price history cannot be reconstructed.

nodes.name: BiasEstimate
nodes.summary: Dataclass recording an estimated survivorship drag with its failure and buyout counts, reconstructed universe size and recovery assumption. Its annual_drag_pct field holds a fraction despite the name; callers multiply by 100 to display it.

nodes.name: DelistingRegistry
nodes.summary: Lazily loads the delisting parquet file and answers date-window and survivorship-drag queries. A missing file logs a warning and yields an empty frame, so the estimate degrades to no correction instead of crashing.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: DelistingRegistry method that returns the cached delisting frame, reading the parquet file on first use and substituting an empty, correctly columned frame with a warning when the file is absent.

nodes.name: bias_estimate
nodes.summary: DelistingRegistry method that computes the annual failure rate over a window against a universe reconstructed by adding delisted names back, then scales it by one minus the assumed recovery. The result is an upper bound for a liquidity-screened strategy.

nodes.name: universe.py
nodes.summary: Pre-declared study testing whether the equal-weight liquid NSE universe beats the Nifty Midcap 100 after costs and survivorship drag, across sub-periods, rolling three-year windows and an investable 40-name version. All three criteria must hold for a PASS; anything less is a FAIL.

nodes.name: IndexDownloadError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when Yahoo Finance returns no prices for an index, which halts the study instead of letting an empty series pass every comparison.

nodes.name: index_returns
nodes.summary: Downloads an index's daily close-to-close returns from Yahoo Finance and raises IndexDownloadError on a failed or empty download, because an empty series would have a zero Sharpe ratio and make the verdict pass.

nodes.name: point_in_time_screen
nodes.summary: Builds daily membership masks for the liquid universe and its most-traded subset from trailing traded value, shifted one day so a stock's membership on day t uses only earlier sessions. This removes the look-ahead of screening on the panel's last year.

nodes.name: over_days
nodes.summary: Restricts a return series to given days so that two Sharpe ratios cover the same window, as criterion (c) requires.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Study entry point that runs _main and turns an IndexDownloadError into a printed stop message and exit code 1, so no conclusion is drawn without the index.

nodes.name: _main
nodes.summary: Runs the full study: builds the screened universe and applies costs and survivorship drag, reports sub-period and size-decomposed Sharpe ratios, rolling three-year windows, and five random-seed 40-name annual backtests, then prints the PASS or FAIL verdict.

nodes.name: test_delisting_registry.py
nodes.summary: Tests the delisting registry against a handmade parquet fixture rather than the NSE file: failure classification, window filtering, drag arithmetic and graceful handling of a missing registry.

nodes.name: registry
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture that writes four handmade delistings to a temporary parquet file and returns a DelistingRegistry backed by it, keeping the suite free of network access.

nodes.name: TestClassification
nodes.summary: Checks that a voluntary delisting is not flagged as a failure and that a liquidation is.

nodes.name: TestWindow
nodes.summary: Checks that in_window keeps only delistings inside the requested dates, excluding those before and after.

nodes.name: TestBiasEstimate
nodes.summary: Checks the drag estimate: separate failure and buyout counts, upward universe reconstruction, positive drag, zero drag at full recovery, scaling with failure share, and a no-correction result when the registry file is missing.

nodes.name: test_universe.py
nodes.summary: Regression tests for the universe study covering three past bugs: a look-ahead liquidity screen, an index compared over the wrong window, and a failed index download that silently passed the verdict.

nodes.name: test_the_universe_on_a_day_uses_only_traded_value_from_before_it
nodes.summary: Regression test confirming a stock enters the screen only the day after its trailing traded value qualifies, and that nothing qualifies on the first day.

nodes.name: test_the_index_is_compared_over_the_portfolios_own_days
nodes.summary: Regression test confirming over_days restricts the index to exactly the portfolio's days.

nodes.name: _NoPrices
nodes.summary: Test double for yfinance.Ticker whose history call returns an empty frame, simulating Yahoo Finance having no prices.

nodes.name: _Unreachable
nodes.summary: Test double for yfinance.Ticker whose constructor raises ConnectionError, simulating a network failure.

nodes.name: test_a_failed_index_download_stops_the_study
nodes.summary: Parametrized regression test confirming index_returns raises IndexDownloadError for both an empty download and an unreachable network.

nodes.name: event_study.py
nodes.summary: Implements the electoral bond event study: three disclosure events, a sector and traded-value matched buyer-minus-control portfolio, and CARs with standard errors taken from the portfolio's own estimation-window variance to avoid cross-sectional correlation.
nodes.languageNotes: Calls pct_change(fill_method=None) so missing prices stay NaN instead of being forward-filled, which is what lets eligible() exclude incomplete stocks.

nodes.name: event_study.py
nodes.summary: Runnable study script behind `python cli.py study event-study`: states the pre-declared decision rules, runs the group-level primary test with a Holm correction across events, prints the pre-publication drift description, and reports entity-level and market-adjusted checks.

nodes.name: test_event_study.py
nodes.summary: Tests the event study on synthetic price panels with a known answer, covering detection of an injected reaction, false positives in noise, control comparability, estimation-window placement, missing prices, and the drift description.

nodes.name: Event
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one disclosure event by key, day-0 date and label.

nodes.name: _positions
nodes.summary: Maps each event key to its integer position in the price index, raising ValueError if an event date is not a trading day.

nodes.name: EventStudy
nodes.summary: Core study engine over a close and volume panel: finds stocks with complete prices, pairs each buyer with a same-sector control closest in log traded value, computes CARs with t-tests and minimum detectable effects, and describes pre-event drift.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Prints one result table of CAR, 95% interval, p-value and minimum detectable effect per event and window.

nodes.name: make_study
nodes.summary: Builds an EventStudy from the price store, the universe and the connected-company set at the given connection level.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds a study at the given connection level and runs it, optionally with the market-adjusted portfolio.

nodes.name: describe_drift
nodes.summary: Prints the output of EventStudy.drift as a description of pre-publication moves, explicitly not a test.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the study: checks the price panel is populated, applies the primary decision rule and Holm correction, prints the drift description and runs the entity-level and market-adjusted checks.

nodes.name: panel
nodes.summary: Generates a synthetic price and volume panel with buyers, others, two sectors, a common market factor and an optional injected event-day jump.

nodes.name: test_detects_a_known_reaction
nodes.summary: Checks that a 3% jump injected on the names event is recovered in the [0,+1] CAR with p below 0.01.

nodes.name: test_finds_nothing_in_noise
nodes.summary: Checks that pure-noise panels across 20 seeds yield at most three false positives at the 5% level.

nodes.name: test_controls_come_from_the_same_sector_once_each
nodes.summary: Checks that every matched control shares its buyer's sector, is unique, and is never itself a connected company.

nodes.name: test_estimation_window_ends_before_the_first_event
nodes.summary: Checks that the estimation window closes before the first event so the event cannot contaminate it.

nodes.name: test_a_stock_with_missing_prices_is_left_out
nodes.summary: Checks that a stock missing a price on an event day is excluded from eligibility and from matching.

nodes.name: test_event_days_must_be_trading_days
nodes.summary: Checks that constructing a study raises ValueError when an event date is absent from the price panel.

nodes.name: test_drift_is_described_for_pairs_whose_buyer_trades_more_and_for_the_rest
nodes.summary: Checks that drift injected into the higher-traded buyers shows up in their pair split and that the whole-portfolio path averages the two halves.

nodes.name: tests.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that runs the project's pytest suite on every push and pull request, using a single ubuntu-latest job on Python 3.11 with pip caching and dependencies from requirements.txt.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project overview reporting five findings from matching 18,871 Indian electoral bonds to NSE-listed companies, all null or not tradable, alongside a log of data-quality bugs fixed across rebuilds. It also maps the pipeline's modules, gives run commands, and states the study's limits.

nodes.name: pytest.ini
nodes.summary: Pytest configuration that restricts collection to the tests directory, skips the virtualenv, data, and results folders, and enforces strict marker registration.
nodes.languageNotes: The --strict-markers option turns an unregistered pytest marker into a collection error rather than a warning, so a mistyped marker cannot silently deselect tests.

nodes.name: requirements.txt
nodes.summary: Exact version pins for the 13 direct Python dependencies (pandas, statsmodels, arch, rapidfuzz, yfinance, and others) that produced the committed outputs in results/ under Python 3.11.

nodes.name: PurchaseData.csv
nodes.summary: Raw electoral bond purchase disclosure with one row per bond (Date of Purchase, Purchaser Name, Denomination), covering 18,871 bonds bought between April 2019 and January 2024. It names buyers only, with no bond numbers linking a purchase to the redeeming party.
nodes.languageNotes: The file contains 336 blank rows that are skipped on load, and purchaser names are free text with spelling variants, so they need entity resolution before use.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Data dictionary giving the contents and provenance of every committed input, including how the company universe is built and how the Yahoo Finance price panel is obtained. A Known limits section records universe coverage gaps, sector-label bias, price-error filtering and audit scope.

nodes.name: companies.csv
nodes.summary: The listed-company universe of 2,645 NSE equities keyed by scrip_code, nse_symbol, ISIN and CIN where known, with sector, industry and listing date. It is a generated table, built from the committed NSE lists, earlier company IDs and earlier sector labels.

nodes.name: company_ids.csv
nodes.summary: Identifier crosswalk of ISIN, NSE symbol, CIN and BSE scrip code for the 1,589 companies in the earlier universe. It lets those companies keep their original key so earlier results stay comparable.

nodes.name: donor_cins.csv
nodes.summary: Reviewed mapping of 29 purchaser name spellings to the CIN and name of the listed company they refer to. It covers donors that the strict name match misses.

nodes.name: match_audit.csv
nodes.summary: Audit log of 276 reviewed purchasers, each recorded as same_company, subsidiary or not_attributed along with the NSE symbol, the relation and a citation. It extends bond attribution beyond the rule-based name matches with sourced decisions.

nodes.name: nifty_total_market.csv
nodes.summary: NSE constituent list of the Nifty Total Market index, with 754 rows of company name, industry, symbol, series and ISIN. It is the main source of sector labels for the company universe.

nodes.name: nse_equity_list.csv
nodes.summary: NSE's full EQUITY_L list of 2,645 equities with symbol, company name, series, listing date, paid-up value, market lot, ISIN and face value. It defines which companies are in the research universe.
nodes.languageNotes: Most column headers in this NSE export carry a leading space (for example ' SERIES'), so readers must strip header names.

nodes.name: sectors_earlier.csv
nodes.summary: The earlier universe's 123 sector and industry labels keyed by ISIN and NSE symbol, with two sector names normalised. It labels the 30 small companies absent from the Nifty Total Market index file.

nodes.name: connections.csv
nodes.summary: Committed table of the 114 NSE-listed companies linked to electoral bond purchases across 11 sectors, one row per company with symbol, bond count, total crore, largest bond, first and last purchase dates, purchasing entities, and a connected flag that is true for 112 of them.

nodes.name: controls.txt
nodes.summary: Output of the controls study comparing the factor model (Sharpe 1.183) with liquidity-only and random 40-name selection from the same universe. Over the longest window the factor trails the random mean (1.307 vs 1.336), its deflated Sharpe of 0.8327 misses the 0.95 bar, and the verdict is not to proceed with it as the primary signal.

nodes.name: event_study.txt
nodes.summary: Event study output of bond buyers' abnormal returns around the Supreme Court verdict, the publication of buyers' names, and the party linkage, at group and entity level. The primary test (names, [0,+1], 103 matched pairs) gives a CAR of +0.37% with p = 0.443, meaning no detectable reaction, with pre-publication drift reported as a description rather than a test.

nodes.name: factor.txt
nodes.summary: Output of the eight-configuration factor grid with net Sharpe, costs, turnover, and drawdown for each run. The best configuration (top20/reb63d/adv1, net Sharpe 1.214) has a bootstrap interval that includes zero and a deflated Sharpe of 0.5994, so the Phase 2 gate reads do not proceed.

nodes.name: lead_lag.txt
nodes.summary: Output of the pre-declared lead-lag grid testing whether bond buyers lead sector peers, against a size-matched placebo arm, at group level, entity level, and with liquidity judged on 2019 traded value. All three runs report no evidence after Holm adjustment, with a smallest detectable weekly coefficient of 0.085 to 0.089.

nodes.name: leadlag_rule.txt
nodes.summary: Output of the tradability test for the size lead-lag, comparing weekly and monthly threshold rules on a peer basket with buy-and-hold after costs. Weekly rules lag buy-and-hold, and the monthly rule's +0.475 Sharpe gap has a paired-bootstrap interval spanning zero, so it does not survive.

nodes.name: universe.txt
nodes.summary: Output of the test of whether the small and mid-cap universe premium is real, covering sub-period Sharpe ratios against the Midcap100, rolling three-year windows, and an investable 40-name annual version. The investable version beats the index, but the premium fails in one sub-period and two of ten windows, so the pre-declared verdict is FAIL.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point that dispatches subcommands for rebuilding the company universe, matching bonds, downloading prices, running studies, regenerating results and resolving CINs. Imports are deferred into each command so a subcommand loads only what it needs.

nodes.name: cmd_connections
nodes.summary: Matches bond purchasers to listed companies, prints coverage figures and the largest buyers, and writes the connections table to results/connections.csv.

nodes.name: cmd_companies
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the listed-company universe by delegating to the build_companies module's main function.

nodes.name: cmd_prices
nodes.summary: Downloads the daily price panel up to the pinned end date, fetching only symbols missing from the store unless every symbol is requested.

nodes.name: cmd_study
nodes.summary: Imports the selected study module dynamically from the STUDIES registry and returns its exit code.

nodes.name: cmd_results
nodes.summary: Regenerates the results directory by writing the connections table, capturing each study's stdout to a text file and saving the figures, stopping at the first failing study.

nodes.name: cmd_visualize
nodes.summary: Generates the interactive HTML graph of company connections and optionally opens it in the browser.

nodes.name: cmd_trials
nodes.summary: Prints the number of logged backtest trials and the range of their net Sharpe ratios, with a warning not to prune the log.

nodes.name: cmd_cins
nodes.summary: Looks up CINs for companies missing one and writes the candidates to results/cin_candidates.csv for manual review, without ever editing companies.csv.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Builds the argparse parser, defining every subcommand with its options and binding each to its handler function.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Configures logging, silences the yfinance logger, parses arguments and runs the selected subcommand handler.

nodes.name: backtest_trials.jsonl
nodes.summary: Append-style JSON Lines log of factor backtest trials, where each record holds a timestamp, the tested parameters (portfolio size, rebalance interval, liquidity floor, weights, slippage, date range) and net and gross performance statistics. It preserves the trial count that the deflated Sharpe ratio is computed against.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the src package; it contains only a comment and defines no code.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the data layer, whose docstring states that the package handles acquisition, resolution and storage and makes no decisions.

nodes.name: cin_resolver.py
nodes.summary: Resolves company names to Corporate Identification Numbers by scraping Zaubacorp search results, filtering to listed companies and verifying candidates by leading word and fuzzy score. It deliberately refuses uncertain matches, because a wrong CIN would credit one company with another's bonds, and it reports transport failures separately from empty results.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes a company name for comparison by unescaping HTML entities, deleting apostrophes and periods, and removing corporate boilerplate words. Deleting rather than spacing apostrophes keeps names like Divi's aligned under the first-token guard.

nodes.name: _first_token
nodes.summary: Returns the first word of an already-normalized name, or an empty string when there is none.

nodes.name: CinMatch
nodes.summary: Dataclass recording one resolution attempt: the query, the CIN if accepted, the matched name, the score, the candidate count and the reason for the outcome.

nodes.name: CinResolver
nodes.summary: Throttled Zaubacorp client that tries progressively looser search strings for a company name and accepts a listed candidate only if its leading word matches exactly and its fuzzy score clears the threshold. Otherwise it returns an unresolved CinMatch stating why, and it distinguishes an unreachable source from a genuine miss.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the research layer, whose docstring describes it as backtesting and statistical validation.

nodes.name: factor_engine.py
nodes.summary: Ranks a liquidity-screened stock universe at a point in time by combining cross-sectionally z-scored residual momentum, short-term reversal and low-volatility factors into a bounded composite. It uses only data at or before the as-of date to avoid look-ahead bias, and its composite weights are deliberately untuned.

nodes.name: _winsorize
nodes.summary: Clips both tails of a series at a given quantile so that one bad print in an illiquid name cannot dominate a z-score.

nodes.name: _zscore
nodes.summary: Computes a winsorized cross-sectional z-score, returning zeros rather than NaN when the cross-section has no usable variance.

nodes.name: FactorSnapshot
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding a ranked universe at one date, including factor scores, universe size and screening rejection counts, with a helper returning the top names by composite score.

nodes.name: FactorEngine
nodes.summary: Computes residual momentum, reversal and low-volatility factors from a price store, screens symbols on history, recency and liquidity, and produces a clipped weighted composite ranking. Beta is estimated on the scoring window so the skipped recent month cannot affect the momentum score.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker that makes the studies directory importable, which the CLI relies on to load study modules by name.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the test suite; it contains only a comment and defines no code.

nodes.name: test_cin_resolver.py
nodes.summary: Offline tests for the name-to-CIN resolver with search mocked out, centered on refusal behavior so that the resolver declines rather than guesses. Covers name normalization, query variant generation, rejected near-matches and successful resolution paths.

nodes.name: StubResolver
nodes.summary: CinResolver subclass that replaces the network search with a canned result table and records the queries it receives.

nodes.name: TestNormalize
nodes.summary: Verifies that name normalization strips corporate boilerplate, treats Ltd and Limited alike and handles empty input.

nodes.name: TestQueryVariants
nodes.summary: Verifies that search variants delete apostrophes, offer a suffix-free form, run from specific to loose, avoid duplicates and omit very short fragments.

nodes.name: TestRefusal
nodes.summary: Verifies that the resolver declines unlisted-only results, one-letter acronym differences, low-scoring same-head candidates, empty results and empty names, while an apostrophe name still matches.

nodes.name: TestResolution
nodes.summary: Verifies successful resolution paths, including exact matches, preferring listed companies over private namesakes, falling through to looser variants, unescaping HTML names and disabling the listed-only filter.

nodes.name: test_factor_engine.py
nodes.summary: Tests for the cross-sectional factor engine that target silent failure modes such as look-ahead, degenerate cross-sections and thin-liquidity names. An in-memory price store and synthetic random-walk panels keep the suite independent of market data.

nodes.name: make_panel
nodes.summary: Generates a seeded random-walk price panel with enough history for every factor.

nodes.name: FakeStore
nodes.summary: In-memory stand-in for PriceStore that deliberately honours as_of in adv_cr, so look-ahead in the liquidity screen fails at unit-test level.

nodes.name: TestScoring
nodes.summary: Verifies that z-scores are standardized, that constant series yield zeros rather than NaN, and that winsorizing clips outliers.

nodes.name: TestFactors
nodes.summary: Verifies the individual factors: reversal sign, low-volatility preference, removal of the common market factor and the skip of the most recent month in residual momentum.

nodes.name: TestEngine
nodes.summary: Verifies end-to-end ranking, composite bounds, exclusion of data after as_of, liquidity and history screens, an error on an empty panel, and weight normalization.

layers.name: Command Line Entry Points
layers.description: The cli.py dispatcher that rebuilds the universe, matches bonds, downloads prices and runs studies, plus the helper script that lists purchasers still needing a manual audit decision.

layers.name: Pre-Declared Studies
layers.description: Runnable study scripts that apply pre-declared decision rules for the lead-lag, event, factor, control, trading-rule and universe tests, and render the README figures.

layers.name: Research Engines
layers.description: Reusable statistical machinery under src/research: lead-lag group construction, the disclosure event study, the factor ranking engine, and the cost-aware backtester with bootstrap and deflated Sharpe metrics.

layers.name: Attribution Core
layers.description: Top-level src modules holding the fixed study constants, the bond-to-company attribution that defines which firms count as connected for every study, and the connection graph built from it.

layers.name: Data Access
layers.description: Loaders and resolvers under src/data that read the bond disclosure and company universe, rebuild companies.csv, resolve CINs, cache the NSE price panel and estimate delisting drag, without making research decisions.

layers.name: Committed Datasets
layers.description: Input tables under data/, including the raw SBI bond disclosure, NSE and Nifty company lists, the reviewed donor-CIN and match-audit tables, and the append-only backtest trial log behind the deflated Sharpe count.

layers.name: Published Results
layers.description: Committed study outputs under results/: the table of bond-linked listed companies and the text reports recording each pre-declared test and its verdict.

layers.name: Test Suite
layers.description: Pytest suite guarding attribution, data loading and study logic with synthetic panels and regression tests for look-ahead, placebo overlap and silent-pass bugs.

layers.name: Project Docs And CI
layers.description: The project README and data dictionary, the pinned dependency list that reproduces the committed results, pytest settings, and the GitHub Actions workflow running the tests.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README, which asks whether Indian companies that bought electoral bonds behaved differently in the stock market. It describes matching all 18,871 disclosed bonds to 2,645 NSE-listed equities, then testing two things: whether buyers' returns lead their peers', and whether their share prices moved when their names became public. Neither effect shows up, and each test reports the smallest effect it could have detected, so read this project as a careful null result rather than a trading system. Keep the idea of pre-declared decision rules in mind, because every later step serves it.

tour.title: Command-Line Entry Point
tour.description: Everything the README describes is launched from cli.py, which has the highest fan-out in the project. Its subcommands rebuild the company universe, match bonds, download prices, run studies, regenerate results and resolve CINs, so its command list doubles as a map of the pipeline. Treat it as the table of contents for the rest of this tour.
tour.languageLesson: Python normally runs imports at the top of a module, but cli.py defers them into each command function. This means a subcommand loads only the libraries it needs, so a light command does not pay the startup cost of a heavy one.

tour.title: Fixed Study Rules
tour.description: Before any data is touched, src/config.py fixes the paths and the rules that define a politically connected company: attribution level, name-match threshold, minimum bond size and price panel end date. It is tied for the most depended-upon file in the graph, because the data loaders, attribution and backtester all read from it. Keeping these choices in one place supports the pre-declared approach from Step 1, since a definition cannot quietly differ between modules.

tour.title: Raw Bond Disclosure
tour.description: The first real input is PurchaseData.csv, the disclosure with one row per bond giving date, purchaser name and denomination. The bonds.py loader turns it into a clean table using the paths from Step 3, and the data dictionary records the provenance and known limits of every committed input. Note one constraint from the start: the file names buyers only, with no bond numbers linking a purchase to the party that redeemed it.

tour.title: Listed Company Universe
tour.description: Bonds need something to match against, and companies.csv supplies the 2,645 NSE equities with their identifiers and sector labels. It is a generated table: build_companies.py rebuilds it from committed lists such as NSE's equity list and the Nifty Total Market constituents, so the universe can be reproduced rather than taken on trust. The companies.py loader then defines each company's identity key as its CIN, else its BSE scrip code, else its ISIN, and that key is what attribution joins on in the next step.

tour.title: Attributing Bonds to Companies
tour.description: This is the heart of the pipeline: connections.py joins the bonds from Step 4 to the universe from Step 5, and its output defines which firms count as connected in every downstream study. It combines strict name matching with two reviewed tables, donor_cins.csv for spellings the strict match misses and match_audit.csv for sourced decisions on subsidiaries and rejected names. The cin_resolver module deliberately refuses uncertain matches, because a wrong CIN would credit one company with another's bonds, and audit_candidates.py lists the purchasers still needing a human decision.

tour.title: The Connected Company Table
tour.description: The attribution from Step 6 is published as results/connections.csv: 114 listed companies across 11 sectors, of which 112 carry the connected flag that the tests use. Each row gives bond count, total crore, largest bond, purchase dates and purchasing entities. The graph.py module presents the same table as a network linking buyers to a single Electoral Bonds node and to their sectors, which makes the concentration of buying easy to see.

tour.title: Prices and Survivorship
tour.description: Knowing who bought bonds is only half of the data; the studies also need returns. The price_store.py module keeps a local Parquet cache of adjusted NSE closes and raw volume from yfinance, removes implausible moves, and serves point-in-time liquidity figures to every study script. Because the panel only contains surviving stocks, delisting_registry.py uses NSE's delisting record to estimate the annual return drag that is missing, so backtests can report how far their figures are overstated.
tour.languageLesson: Parquet is a columnar file format that stores each column together with its type. That makes it a good cache for wide price panels, since a read can load only the columns it needs and keeps numeric and date types intact, unlike CSV.

tour.title: Peer Lead-Lag Test
tour.description: With connections from Step 7 and prices from Step 8, the first hypothesis can be tested: do bond buyers' returns lead their sector peers'? The research module splits each sector into connected, size-matched placebo and peer groups, removing placebo leaders from the peers so a group cannot predict itself, and the study script fits four frequency and lag specifications with period-clustered errors and Holm adjustment. Notice the pattern of a reusable engine in src/research paired with a runnable script in studies/, which repeats in the next steps. The committed output reports no evidence after adjustment, with a smallest detectable weekly coefficient of 0.085 to 0.089.

tour.title: Disclosure Event Study
tour.description: The second hypothesis asks whether buyers' prices moved when the information became public, across three disclosure events: the Supreme Court verdict, the publication of buyers' names and the party linkage. Following the same engine-and-script split as Step 9, the research module builds a buyer-minus-control portfolio matched on sector and traded value, and takes standard errors from that portfolio's own estimation-window variance to avoid cross-sectional correlation. The primary test on the names event gives a CAR of +0.37% with p = 0.443 over 103 matched pairs, meaning no detectable reaction.

tour.title: Factor Backtesting Machinery
tour.description: Alongside the two bond tests sits a general backtesting stack that later steps depend on. The factor_engine.py module ranks a liquidity-screened universe on residual momentum, reversal and low volatility using only data up to the as-of date, while factor_backtest.py adds NSE delivery costs, T+1 execution, the block-bootstrap Sharpe interval and the deflated Sharpe ratio. Every trial is appended to backtest_trials.jsonl because the deflated Sharpe needs an honest count of how many configurations were tried.
tour.languageLesson: JSON Lines stores one complete JSON object per line. A new record can be appended without parsing or rewriting the existing file, which suits a log whose earlier entries should not change.

tour.title: Factor Validation Gates
tour.description: These two studies put the machinery from Step 11 through staged proceed-or-stop gates. The factor study runs a pre-declared grid of eight configurations, and its best net Sharpe of 1.214 has a bootstrap interval that includes zero and a deflated Sharpe of 0.5994, so the gate reads do not proceed. The controls study then asks whether factor selection beats liquidity-only and random picks from the same universe; over the longest window it trails the random mean, 1.307 against 1.336. The lesson is that an attractive headline Sharpe is not accepted until it survives comparison with these baselines.

tour.title: Tradability and Universe Premium
tour.description: The last two studies ask whether anything left over could actually be earned. The lead-lag rule trades a peer basket only after liquid leaders rose and compares the result after costs with buy-and-hold of that basket; its monthly +0.475 Sharpe gap has a paired-bootstrap interval spanning zero. The universe study tests the equal-weight liquid universe against the Nifty Midcap 100 after costs and the survivorship drag from Step 8, and because all three criteria must hold for a PASS, a failure in one sub-period and two of ten rolling windows yields FAIL.

tour.title: Tests Against Silent Failures
tour.description: A research pipeline can be wrong while still running cleanly, so the test suite targets the specific ways earlier steps could mislead. The universe tests pin three past bugs, including a look-ahead liquidity screen and a failed index download that silently passed the verdict, while the lead-lag tests keep placebo leaders disjoint from peers and the event-study tests inject a known reaction into synthetic panels. The resolver tests check the refusal behavior from Step 6, so that it declines rather than guesses.
tour.languageLesson: Strict marker registration in pytest.ini makes an unregistered marker an error. A mistyped marker name therefore fails loudly at collection instead of being accepted without effect.

tour.title: Reproducing and Presenting Results
tour.description: The tour closes with what keeps the findings repeatable and visible. The requirements file pins the exact versions that produced the committed results under Python 3.11, and the GitHub Actions workflow runs the tests from Step 14 on every push and pull request. The figures.py module draws on the studies and engines from earlier steps to regenerate the README's charts, which brings you back to the findings you read in Step 1.
tour.languageLesson: In a GitHub Actions workflow, the `on` key lists the events that trigger it and each job runs its `steps` in order on the chosen runner. Caching pip downloads between runs shortens dependency installation.
